Use of Language
An adjective is a word that describes a noun or a pronoun. They allow for the description of
what they are modifying, therefore forming a more vivid image of what is being described.
Quantitative Adjective shows how much of anything is described. It is further divided into;
Definitive: It shows an exact number like one, two, second etc.
Example: I have been here for over four and a half billion years.
Indefinite: It shows the quantity which is not an exact count like all, few, several, some,
many, certain etc.
Example: Some of you keep me protected.
Distributive: It shows a specific number out of a group, such as each, every, neither, etc
Example:Each one of us should protect nature.
